INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
1
Introduction
Hey there, I am vaibhav patel, BTech CE student of VJTI (2020 - 2024). I would like to share
you my interview experience for Goldman Sachs Internship opportunity (summer analyst).
I hope my experience is going to help you prepare better for internship and FTE (full time
employment). My interview was a little different from others, It might not be the case with
you!
There were 3 interview rounds and Online assessment. I will share as much as I remember.
2
Online Assesment (30 mins)
Online asssesment had 4 sections, here I am listing them in order. Everyone had the same
questions in all sections in OA :).
2.1
Coding section
It had two problems.
2.1.1
Maximum sum submatrix of size k x k
Football ground is represented by a matrix and each player had a skill on the ground, we
had to find a square part of the ground with side k which had highest average skill. This is
a matrix problem in 2D, refer this maximum sum submatrix.
See the above example, n = 4. if k = 1 then 10.00 will be the answer. if k = 2, 28/4 =
7.00 will be the answer (top right corner 2 x 2 matrix). answer has to be rounded of to two
decimal places. I don’t remember if it was told that skill cannot be negative.
I was able to pass all the test cases 11/11. I wrote the source code in python (I use
both c++ and python). question was medium level according to me. It required a thorough
understanding of kadane’s algorithm and its appplication in 2D array.
2

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
It could have been solved by using the concept of prefix sum matrix. and then going
through all the submatrix of size k x k to find maximum sum submatrix. refer to this prefix
sum matrix. It’s time complexity will be O(n2) (equivalent to time for taking matrix input).
I would suggest you to solve the problem using this approach because concept of prefix sum
matrix can be used to solve many matrix problems.
2.1.2
catch the thief
This problem was not similar to standard problems. No one could completely solve it because
of time constraint.
We were given a threshold(thief’s skill and bike power) as the power of the thief. We
were given bikes array and skills array of guards and had to find all combinations of them
so that each of the guards have skill greater than or equal to that of theif.
input:
theif skill = 2
theif bike power = 4
guards skill array = [2, 1, 3]
guards bike array = [4, 3, 6]
output:
0
In the above example there will be zero combinations because guard with 1 skill doesn’t
find a bike so that their power crosses the threshold.
input:
theif skill = 2
theif bike power = 4
guards skill array = [2, 4, 3]
guards bike array = [4, 3, 6]
output:
4
In the above example only the combinations having (2, 3) as a pair will fail the test.
Do you understand something from examples that I have taken? in both of them answer
significantly depends on the smallest element in the array. By this I got the intution to solve
this problem similar to what we do in counting inversions using merge sort. basically if (2,
4) satisfies the threshold then we can say that any number greater than 2 in the first place
will also satisfy the threshold.
sort both arrays
skills = [2, 3, 4]
bikes = [3, 4, 5]
keep a variables answer as = 1, start iterating from start of first array (you can do with
second array) and find the point where the threshold is first satisfied (use binary search for
better time complexity), in our case when we are at element 2 the first element in second
array will be 4, multiply (n - isecond - ifirst) to the multiplier, where ifirst is the index of
element in first array, isecond is the index that we found using binary search, (3 - 1 - 0) will
3

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
be multiplied with the multiplier variable. basically we are finding all possible combinations
for the first element in the array, subtracting ifirst is important because one of the possible
pair will be taken by the previous element in the first array (all possible pairs of previous
element will be subset of next element because next element is greater than previous. It is
similar to what we do in permutations), (n - secondindex) is the number of elements that
satisfy the combination. for the element 3, ifirst = 1, isecond = 0 so again (3 - 0 - 1) = 2
will be multiplied to the variable. for element 4 in the first array ifirst = 2, isecond = 0 so
multiplier will be multiplied by (3 - 0 - 2) = 1. so finally the variable will be 4 which is the
correct answer.
in the first example the multiplier for element 1 will be multiplied with (3 - 0 - 3) = 0
and answer will become zero. binary search will result end pointer which is at 1 + possible
index of the array. similarly for any such case the variable will become zero whenever we
find a point where there are no possibilities.
I was able to pass 7/12 test cases, actually I forgot to sort the second array and when
I was modifying the code time ended. I don’t think so anyone solved this problem. I was
very happy that I was able to intuitively solve the problem. question was medium level but
it wasn’t DSA type instead it was CP type.
2.2
Aptitude test: 40-45 mins
It had some 12 questions I guess and all of them were math baased JEE questions. I was
really happy because I gave JEE advanced in first year so I can solve all of them. I would
like to share some questions that I remember. Negative marking of -2 was there.
2.2.1
Geometric progression
the sum of 3 terms in GP and product of them was given and we had to find those 3 terms.
so we have to assume three terms and solve equations
a
r + a + ar = S
a
r · a · ar = M
solving the second equation we get the value of a and then substituting in 1 we get quadratic
equation in r. on solvin that we get the 3 terms.
2.2.2
Order extraction
This kind of questions are standard in aptitude test. given some conditions on a specific
objects ordering we have to find the position at which a specific object is. You will require
pen and paper to model the current position after each condition, Practice those questions
because it was also there in morgan stanley test.
a short example:
1) A is at left of D
2) B is after D
3) C is at the start.

CADB
2.2.3
Probability with 2 boxes
This is also a standard type of aptitude question. 2 boxes will contain 2 types of colored
boxes and probability of specific color ball has to be found following the given constraints.
focus on the with or without replacement part. refer to Indiabix for aptitude questions.
2.2.4
Probability involving infinite GP
There are types of questions which require infinite GP formula to be solved. they are involved
in 2 player games. There was a similar question in test.
there are two players, player wins if he gets the tail for the first time.
what is the

Summary
I don’t think so you will be able to solve all the questions, just make sure you do not mark
wrong answers at any cost because this section had negative marking -2 and +5 for positive
answer. a wrong answer can be a -7 for you wasting your +5 time and causing you -2.
2.3
HR essay questions; 15 mins
I will not elaborate a lot about this section it had two HR questions.
 Your biggest achievement
 Given a situation(a member is not devoted to his work) in your team, what will you
do?
Try to keep those answers as gentle as possible. Don’t try to write unnecessary things
and it should be formally written. Don’t be extremely strict or very polite in your answer.
These questions are going to represent your personality. In achivement include your entrance
score (maybe CET) or anything that you feel was at a national/state level so that they can
5

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
understand the level of competition. You can include programming contests and hackathon
if you want.
2.4
CS fundamentals: 20 mins
This part contained CS fundamental questions based on OOPS, CN (computer networks),
DBMS, DSA etc. there were only 7 questions with +5 -2 marking. I would like to share
couple of them:
2.4.1
Topology in computer networks
There was a question which was based on concept of topology in computer networks. We
were not aware of any such questions. Google baba came to our rescue :). Answer was star
topology I don’t remember the question.
2.4.2
Linked List
Here comes a tricky questions which will trap you if you haven’t read the question correctly.
they were printing the linked list using a while loop but while printing they had
cout << node −> next −> data << endl;
instead of
cout << node −> data << endl;
at each step in the while loop
node = node −> next −> next;
so if the linked list was 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 then 2, 4, 6 was the correct answer.
Many people just selected 1, 3, 5 as the answer not reading what they are printing. I
observed it correctly and marked the right answer. I will advice you to read the code and
question with full focus.
2.5
Overall summary
Online assessment of goldman sachs was best among all the online assessments. It is going
to be a good experience for you and there are high chances of your selection. make sure you
have a friend named chatGPT :), we didn’t have it.
6

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
3
Interview Round 1
After the online assessment total of 36 people got selected for interviews (It is a huge number).
Also, 18 boys and 18 girls were selected (I observed the count). So, if you are a boy your
competition is going to be with only boys and vice versa. Similarly prepare for the internship
test.
As there were total of 36 students they divided them in three sections and told each of
us to seat according to the sections in 3 column of benches in TPO hall. one by one they
started calling names of people.
3.1
Round 1: Technical 40 mins
As there were many people in each section, my turn came late. When I entered the interview
cabin, interviewer(she) asked me your interview is starting late, how are you feeling? and I
said I like to keep patience in my life, I am feeling good. She was impressed. Also, I wore
formals with tie, I was confident in communication and body language. (I think from that
point I knew that my interview is going to be amazing!). I will list the questions now as
subsection:
3.1.1
Questions on project
She was reading my resume, and I had mentioned one project based on machine learning
to predict the probable prize in future using custom design model. I was working on that
project at that time, I only had the knowledge of project idea but I don’t know why in each
interview they told me to explain this project. I think goldman is a financial firm and stock
market comes under it’s own matter of interest so they interogatted me on the project in
each interview.
She told me to explain how is your model going to work?
(basically a dry run).
I
explained her with an example stock and representing the graph of prize vs time. I then
explained the working of the model on how it is going to use the curvature of the graph
to predict future. Also, I mentioned the different cases for sudden increase and decrease of
stock prizes (news of company, AGM, Quarter report).
What is the dataset you are using to train the model? was the next question. I answered,
I will be using historical stock prizes data of last one year of NSE/BSE for training and test
it on the last one month data.
What API you are using for fetching the stock market data? I replied with yahoo finance
API and its python library implementation. I don’t know if she was known to this.
She had some more questions and I answered all of them. Almost, 20 mins passed just
during the project questions. It was advantageous for me because I was totally known to my
project implementation.
7

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
3.1.2
DSA Questions
After a lot of time drain in questions about project, now it was the time of DSA. She asked
me total of 3 questions on DSA
1. Maximum length subarray having sum k.
This question have many different solutions including prefix sum, sliding window, dy-
namic programming, I was unsure which one should I use. I first started with brute
force approach iterating through all arrays and finding maximum length subarray hav-
ing given sum k. I used max heap to store the maximum length (I don’t know why
:)) making the complexity O(n2 log n). She told me you can use a variable instead of
heap and I agreed to her. making the complexity O(n2). She told me to optimize then
I choose sliding window approach and did a dry run on test array with pen and paper.
question was quiet easier for me and I was happy that I was lucky.
2. Print all the nodes of k-ary tree This was a kind of weird question, she told me that in a
folder you need to print names of all directories, files inside it (names of all, irrespective
of the depth of it). basically she wanted me to write traversal for graph (it was not a
binary tree). I did it with BFS, did a dry run and was successfully able to solve this
problem too.
3. Morris traversal: Tree traversal with O(1) auxiliary space. Next question was again
based on tree. tree traversal with O(1) auxiliary space. I was little confused about
the algorithm, how we are storing the previous and next link and how it has to be
implemented. I acted like I didn’t know about any such algorithm because if I would
have tried, I would have failed to explain it completely. I kept on bubbling around
BFS and DFS. After some time she told me to stop.
3.1.3
Do you have any questions?
After almost 35-40 mins of interview she finally asked me whether do you have any question
about us.
I questions what do you do at GS. she replied as she works as frontend lead and devel-
ops project in NextJS. I added to that next is so good and also the functional component,
React class components are so difficult to understand having methods like getDerivedState-
FromProps,componentDidMount, shouldComponentUpdate etc. She then asked the ques-
tion about react class component in next interview :) and that guy couldn’t answer. I would
suggest not to do what I did, The extra knowledge you may have may not be known to
others.
I also asked if there are some opportunities for machine learning at GS? she told me
your work will depend on your team. Usually interns don’t get to work on machine learning
projects.
Here my first interview was over, I knew that I will make it to second round. While
leaving the cabin I took the notebook given by her with me. After reaching TPO hall I came
to know about this and went back to her and gave that book (she was also laughing :)))).
8

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
3.2
Round 2: HR + technical 35-40 mins
After 5 mins of completion of interview I was called for second interview. This was kind
of weird interview and the interviewer was a NIT trichy CS graduate of 2007 who also did
internship at GS and working there for more than 15 years (After coming here at GS I met
him and learnt more about him, he was hosting one of the events at GS with a global head
of our department asking him questions).
3.2.1
Questions on project
He also liked my machine learning project and told me to explain about it. I explained the
same thing to him, which I explained in first interview.
He asked a really good question on the project, Will you change your Machine learning
model if you are making investment from other country to India? I understood the concept
that he saw the russia vs ukraine war in the news and wanted to know If I am aware of
the impact of foreign exchange. I answered yes model will need to be altered according to
the exchange, If your country’s exchange rate is higher on a particular date than normal, It
will be profitable even if the prize of stock doesn’t change and you sell on the same prize in
Indian market. So for example, If I am in japan and japanese currency(yen) exchange rate
is X + k INR for some day, if I buy some stokes of INR then I will need to pay
Y
X + k yen.
If the exchange rate again become X at some day in India, I can sell the stocks at same prize
Y but I will be in profit because the sell amount will be Y
X yen which is more than the buy
price. So, model needs to be altered. he liked my answer. He also asked a little question
about the last project in my resume which was kind of dynamic calculator, I answered that
too.
Then he asked me whether all the projects are implemented by me alone? I said yes, I
have worked on all projects alone. He liked that I learnt lot of techstacks in almost 8 months.
It shows my grasping power (this was sadly because I was kind of absent at college since I
was giving JEE advanced in first year and it almost took my first 3 sems without learning
about programming. But It was worth because I got good score and AIR rank 6913, which
is going to be there in my resume forever. On that day I failed to score good marks in paper
1(I was little sick because of change in environment because of monsoon), because of which
I again couldn’t get CSE again but I still don’t regret my decision and happy about that.
It is always a proud moment to say that you were ahead of more than 50% of those who
qualify for most difficult examination of India for engineering).
3.2.2
HR type question
Where do you rank yourself? was the next question. Again this is a weird question to answer
comparing yourself with friends. I answered him that I may not be the best programmer
here having the most experience but Aptitude wise I can outshine many. I gave my CP
codechef rating (4 star coder) and JEE advanced rank as a justification. At that time I was
the only 4 star coder in the CE branch, I mentioned that (in the vacation, I gave all the
contests and was able to reach 4 star). He again liked my answer.
9

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
What was your favourite mathematics concept during JEE prep? I answered with calculus
(I choose calculus because it has extensive use everywhere). Then one more weird question,
How will you explain calculus to a 5 year old child? (At that moment I felt like whattt). I
immediately answered the question with I will tell him that see how is your height changing
each year. Kids always have so much interest in their height (I also had, I always felt like
our height changes on our birthdays :)))). So I will tell him to keep track of his height and
define the change in height with respect of time in years as rate measure. he liked my answer
a lot and told makes sense. This question was kind of a puzzle to me.
3.2.3
Puzzle
I had not prepared any puzzle questions, I was not known to any puzzle. He first asked me If
I know about 9 ball puzzle? I answered no. He explained me what the question is: basically
there are 9 balls on a table and a weighing machine (not the digital one, one with two side
on which we can keep weights and compare the weights of two objects). one of the ball has
slight different weight may be more or may be less, I have to find that ball from them using
that weighing machine. for example:
1, 1.01, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1
can be the weights of 9 balls, I had no knowledge of this problem. First approach that I
came up with was to check each consecutive pairs in the weighing machine in order. (1, 2), (2,
3) . . . there will be a moment when weighing machine show will deflection for two consecutive
pairs and we will find the second ball of first pair as answer. total of n operations has to be
performed (n = 9).
Second approach that I came up with was to compare each pair without intersection,
select the pair which shows deflection and compare the each ball of that pair with the
remaining ball (9 th ball). If no pair shows the deflection 9 th ball is the answer. (1, 2), (3,
4), (5, 6), (7, 8). the ball from odd pair which shows the deflection with last ball will be the
answer. this approach had n/2 operations.
he was still expecting more optimized, I finally understood it required the divide and
conquer approach. we will weigh first 4 balls with last 4 balls, if there is no deflection,
middle ball is answer. else seperate each 4 balls to 2-2 and weigh, the one which still shows
deflection that group contains the odd ball. This process had to be followed recursively.
finally comparing one ball of the final pair to remaining ball finding the answer. see the
below steps
 1 + 1.01 + 1 + 1 != 1 + 1 + 1 + 1
 1 + 1.01 != 1 + 1 and 1 + 1 == 1 + 1
 1 != 1.01 and 1 == 1
here we found the defective pair and now we compare one ball with remaining 1 ball,
if we choose 1.01 randomly, weighing machine will shaw deflection. so it will be the
answer. If we choose 1, machine will show no deflection, therefore the other ball will
be answer.
Interviewer was satisfied with my problem solving skills.
10

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
3.2.4
What do you know about GS and why would you like to join GS?
I was unaware about goldman sachs as a firm so I didn’t have any good knowledge of that
but thankfully I attended the PPT (pre placement talk). I answered that goldman sachs is a
big firm and stands at good position in financial market. I mentioned that we have globally
around 150 centers which I like. I mentioned that goldman sachs is second best firm (in
terms of compensation) after DE shaw at VJTI (I shouldn’t have mentioned this :)). He was
smiling at this moment and asked me what happened to your DE shaw interview? (maybe
he just wanted to know). I told him that morgan stanley interview was on the same day as
the online assessment, since I was rejected in the interview of morgan stanley I didn’t give
DE shaw test seriously. I wasn’t selected for interview at DE shaw. I also mentioned that
in morgan stanley interview I was asked some out of the box questions which I didn’t know.
He told me what were they? Do you know answers of them now? This was again shocker
to me I said yes, I mentioned the question of OS what are cores in? how it is different from
processor? I also answered about it. This concept will be there in the parallel computing in
Third year so I wasn’t aware of that. Interviewer was happy from my answer.
3.2.5
Do you have any questions?
After asking lot of questions interviewer himself said I asked you a lot of questions, Do you
have any questions for me? (Huhh finally I felt relief). I said what was your journey to
goldman sachs? he said I was NIT trichy CS graduate and working in GS since then (He
didn’t mention when did he join, I was impressed with that since NIT trichy CS is the most
difficult to get into through JEE mains in current era). I was exclaimed and also told if
he ever switched his company, he said no. (After coming here I learnt that why he didn’t
change).
3.2.6
Summary
This will be one of the weirdest interview I would have had. I developed a good connection
with him in here at the firm during internship, I will even choose him for reviewing my
project. Remember that interviewers are the first point of contact with the firm. I will
mention a little at the end about my interviewers.
11

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
3.3
Round 3: Technical 40 mins
I went out of the cabin for seating in the TPO hall, but just in that time one person came
and called my name for the 3rd interview (at that moment I felt like whattt). I was the
second who was called for 3 rd interview, there were people who didn’t go for second round
and there were people whose second round was the last round taken by GS before they
announced we are done! It doesn’t matter how many interviews you will need to give before
getting selected (I felt weird since my first interview was too late).
Third interviewr was the guy that sits on the same floor with me few meters away and
he works in my department in one of the sister teams. I met him one day and told him you
took my 3rd interview and he recognized me. I had a good talk with him. let us see what
was there in the final interview:
3.3.1
Questions on project
He also asked me to give the short introduction about that machine learning project (he also
told everyone would have asked you about this, explain in short). he had some questions
and I answered them.
I was using both PostgreSQL and MongoDB in one of my project (news website with
chatbot). He asked why am I using both postgreSQL and MongoDB in the same project,
what is the need? I tried to answer this question theoretically like MongoDB can be used to
store unstructured data like chats of people and postgreSQL will be good for serial informa-
tion like personal information. He wasn’t happy with the answer he kept on asking what is
the need of both, they can be done in one place. Finally, I mentioned that joins is something
that we can perform only in SQL (postgreSQL) so that we can retrieve the information from
multiple tables. He finally liked that point and said ya this can be a correct reason for using
both type of databases (stay calm in such situations).
3.3.2
Google hashcode
I had mentioned that I solved google hashcode problem statement in one of my achievements.
He wanted to know about the problem and how I solved it (I was the only one at that time
to have that problem solved in SY). I explained him the problem statement, It was a kind
of team formulation problem and I explained the solution which I wrote in python. I also
mentioned that I solved problem in only 62 lines. scoring a descent score on the 2 test cases.
I think so he liked that.
3.3.3
Puzzles
After some 20 mins interviewer told me that let us go to DSA now, are you good with DSA?
I was kind of not happy and wasn’t sure of answering question. so he said that 3 puzzles or
3 DSA questions. I said puzzles (I was kind of very happy because puzzles is something that
I like because I can solve them). Maybe you do not get the option that I got :)). (DSA is
better because you at least you know about it, but I was not master of DSA). I will list all
the puzzles next
12

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
 Two poles and cable puzzle
This was a standard problem which I was not aware of, You can refer to this link: two
poles and a cable
there are two poles of height 15 meters and a string of 16 meters, initially string is tight
and we start moving poles towards each other, at some point height of the lowest point
on string from ground is 7 meter. what is the distance between the poles at that time?
(this was the exact question asked by the interviewer). I felt like it will include some
parabola kind of stuff so I told him that writing the equation of parabola can solve
the question. At some point I used the unitary method to just get some idea about
the range of answer (height from ground will be directly proportional to the distance
between poles, this was the concept that I got as a intuition). Mathematically,
16 = 15
x = 7
when I wrote this I also tried to find some correlation between the numbers. 15 - 7 =
8 looked a divisor of 16 and then I found the answer.
basically at 8x2 = 16 will be the total string which will be straight when the distance
between poles become zero. So, I got the correct answer. Interviewer told me to explain
me how did I get the answer (I tried to explain this and then he said let us move to
second puzzle).
13

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
 N meetings problem
This was a kind of a standard problem. Interviewer explained this with some story
but I was able to explain the concept well. It was a greedy algorithm, I would not
elaborate a lot about this. Refer to this link: N meetings problem. He also told me to
do a dry run. He represented this problem to me as a puzzle but it was a kind of DSA
problem.
 N squares problem
I knew that this might be the last thing in my interview. I wanted to solve this problem
but the question was difficult. We have to divide a square into k distinct square (there
are no constraint on length od square, we just need to divide it into k squares). I would
like you to refer this question here: N square problem
I tried to solve it for enough time, I was trying to find the possible solution for n = 5 but
this problem is not solvable for n = 2, 3, 5 (I don’t remember if he said the constraints
of the problem). This problem remained in my head for many days, thinking about
different possible ways to solve the problem.
After 5-7 mins interviewer told me its okay you can go, I said sorry for that I can’t
solve this problem (I don’t know why :))). I asked him for the solution and he said that
there is a technique you can check online, he beforehand mentioned its okay if I cannot
solve this problem. Anyways I knew that I will be surely selected from interviews.
3.4
Summary
Kuddos to you if you have reached here reading my interview experience, I hope you enjoyed
reading my interview and now feeling relaxed (I hope).
Second interviewer was in AWM public (I am in AWM private) department. It is very
important to make good connection here (we have been told the word networking 100 times
in all sessions, had a networking dinner and lunch). Make sure that you have good impact
on the interviewers, so that you can connect with them once you are doing internship. 3 rd
interviewer is just my neighbour (yesterday we had lunch in the cafeteria on same table). 2
nd interviewer told me that they hired me for AWM.
14

INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
Vaibhav patel
4
Resources
I wouldn’t like to waste your time representing all resources but I will explain just the
important once
1. Geeks for geeks
This is a kind of bhagwad geeta for preparation, Also now they have improvised the
level of content and day by day working on it. for all CS fundamentals you must
read GFG articles in the topics of that subject on GFG. GFG is also good for DSA
practice. search ”Data structures GFG” on google to get all the data structures and
related questions. search ”GFG algorithms” to find the reference containing all types
of algorithms, time complexity anlysis, practice problems.
2. medium.com This is the website which I like the most. Articles here are of very good
level and you will find an article for any topic. Search top 50 DP questions medium
and you will get an article having 50 good DP problems with their solution links.
3. interviewbit
This is also kind of concise resource of end moment preparation. search ¡subject¿ top
50 questions interview bit and you will get list of most important questions for that
subject. Believe me this is going to be very helpful.
4. Indiabix

Tips and Motivation
Here I would like to list the most important tips and tricks:
1. Confidence is the key to success.
2. Be sure of what you are saying, confusion is poison.
3. Focus on your skills, don’t create chaos at the end moment.
4. Don’t be demotivated, It’s not the end. Sun of next day might be even brighter.
5. Don’t mug up DSA, give CP contests (It is like after learning DSA you must be able
to solve problems in CP, may not be faster).
6. Don’t Lie on stuff that you know interviewer don’t know, Lie at your own risk (on your
projects).
7. Behave well with them, wear formal cloths.
8. Always ask them something after the interview.
9. Sleep well before the day of interview.
10. Remember it’s not only you who need the firm, but firm also needs you (if you are
talented).
11. Remember your mistakes, forget your achievements.
12. Don’t answer sarcastically, answer practically.
13. You are never fully prepared for interview, It depends on how much you are sure of
what you have learnt.
14. Don’t be a monkey, we are improvised version of them (don’t copy what others are
doing).
15. It’s you who will define your future!!
With this I will end my interview experience here, I hope you never felt boring throughout
the interview. (I have shared some info that I didn’t want but I hope you will make use of
it, don’t laugh on me :))). Remember that you need to write your interview experience just
after the interview :))).
All The Best!!
